problems.title: Kernel A
problems.statement: Kernel time / wall time per launch: 0.90. SOL: DRAM 88%, L2 60%, issue 20%, tensor 0%. FMA share of issued instructions: 10%.
hints: Launch check, then the busiest unit, then the 60% line, then the FMA share.
problems.solution: Bandwidth-bound. Coalesce, reuse or shrink the data: bytes are the cost.

problems.title: Kernel B
problems.statement: Kernel time / wall time per launch: 0.90. SOL: DRAM 22%, L2 25%, issue 30%, tensor 0%. FMA share of issued instructions: 20%.
hints: Launch check, then the busiest unit, then the 60% line, then the FMA share.
problems.solution: Latency-bound. Nothing is saturated: more warps or more independent loads (Little's law).

problems.title: Kernel C
problems.statement: Kernel time / wall time per launch: 0.30. SOL: DRAM 10%, L2 10%, issue 10%, tensor 0%. FMA share of issued instructions: 30%.
hints: Launch check, then the busiest unit, then the 60% line, then the FMA share.
problems.solution: Launch-bound. The GPU waits for launches: fuse kernels or use CUDA Graphs.

problems.title: Kernel D
problems.statement: Kernel time / wall time per launch: 0.95. SOL: DRAM 30%, L2 40%, issue 90%, tensor 0%. FMA share of issued instructions: 20%.
hints: Launch check, then the busiest unit, then the 60% line, then the FMA share.
problems.solution: Issue-bound. Mostly overhead instructions: vector loads, register tiling, fix bank conflicts.

problems.title: Kernel E
problems.statement: Kernel time / wall time per launch: 0.95. SOL: DRAM 35%, L2 45%, issue 92%, tensor 0%. FMA share of issued instructions: 85%.
hints: Launch check, then the busiest unit, then the 60% line, then the FMA share.
problems.solution: Compute-bound. FP32 is full: tensor cores or lower precision.

problems.title: The bottleneck moves
problems.statement: A kernel is bandwidth-bound at 88% DRAM SOL taking 2.0 ms. You cut its DRAM bytes in half.

parts.prompt: New time if it stays bandwidth-bound, in ms?
Its issue work alone takes 1.4 ms. Actual new time, at best, in ms?

hints: Time is set by the slowest unit.
problems.solution: Halving bytes would give 1.0 ms, but issue needs 1.4 ms: the kernel becomes issue-bound at 1.4 ms (1.43×, not 2×). Re-diagnose after every fix.

problems.title: A kernel above 60% on two units

options: Mixed: near both limits, so fixing one alone gains little

parts.prompt: Upper bound on the speedup from fixing memory alone?

hints: Time can't drop below the other unit's share.
problems.solution: Both units are near saturation; removing all memory pressure leaves issue at 70% of the current time, so about 1.03×. Such kernels need a restructuring that cuts both (fusion, better tiling).

problems.title: Little's law diagnosis
problems.statement: A latency-bound copy kernel on the GW-1 reaches 30% of peak bandwidth at 25% occupancy, one 128-byte request per warp.

parts.prompt: Warps resident on the whole GPU?
Predicted fraction of peak, in %, from Little's law (136,533 bytes needed)?
Requests per warp needed for 100% at this occupancy?

problems.solution: (a) 25% of 1,024 = 256 warps. (b) 24%, close to the measured 30%: the model explains the kernel. (c) 5 requests per warp (unroll the loop, or float4 loads): no occupancy change needed.

problems.title: Tensor cores, starved
problems.statement: After moving a GEMM to tensor cores: tensor SOL 35%, DRAM 40%, L2 45%, issue 30%. Occupancy 25%, top stall: long scoreboard.

options: Deeper pipelining (more stages in flight) or bigger tiles

problems.solution: Latency-bound: the math got 8× faster and the loads didn't. Keep more loads in flight (double or triple buffering, cp.async) so the tensor units are fed. This is exactly the step in Part 4 after tensor cores.

problems.title: Evidence before change
problems.statement: Your teammate says: "It's slow because of bank conflicts."

options: MIO throttle or short-scoreboard stalls dominate
Issue SOL high with a low FMA share

hints: Conflicts inflate shared-memory work and issue slots.
problems.solution: Conflicts show as extra wavefronts, MIO/short-scoreboard stalls, and issue time spent on non-math. High DRAM SOL points elsewhere.
